title: Human gorpse–corpse frame: 10 ms nominal delay
scope: Actual human speech with deleted aspiration; new teaching continuum, not original study tokens.
note: New teaching reconstruction from the actual US-English recording of corpse by Dvortygirl. Each member retains the complete 10 ms native release complex and the same entire native periodic vowel, rhotic segment and coda. Different amounts of middle aspiration are deleted from the real recording, retaining 10–70 ms nominal release-to-common-rhyme intervals in 5 ms steps. All audible material comes from that one human recording; no Kokoro, generated buzz, random aspiration, voice cloning or vocoder is used. These are not Ganong (1980) original stimuli, and no perceptual category boundary or endpoint identification is independently established. Uniform quiet playback gain is shared by the family; 150 ms leading/trailing silence is added around individual words.
credit: Original corpse recording by Dvortygirl (2006), Wikimedia Commons. New aspiration-deletion edits and listening assembly for LING406.
